For me, the fullscreen start menu is a lot easier to use. It has big, easy to see and press icons, you don't have to move your mouse and eyes to the bottom left corner after hitting the Windows key, you can store a whole lot more apps on it, you can have a weather widget (tile), and you can still just start typing to search for a program. All those benefits make me wonder, why do people hate the fullscreen start menu on Windows 8 and optional on Windows 10?

EDIT: Sure I know people hate metro apps, I do too, but you don't have to use them to enjoy the benefits to the Start menu.
ELI5: [Windows] Why do people hate the fullscreen start menu so much
Because people like to be able to see what programs/files they already have up when they're in the start menu.
How? Whenever I've opened up the start menu, it shows frequently used apps and pinned apps, but never apps that are currently open. Also, doesn't the taskbar do that?

you don't have to move your mouse and eyes to the bottom left corner after hitting the Windows key

No, but you do have to move your eyes to the bottom of the screen when you do a right-click on anything in the Start Screen, which is moronic.

In addition, because you can't see anything else when the Start Screen is up, it's impossible to click-and-drag anything to or from the Start Menu like you can in any system other than Windows 8.

I think they did fix a lot in Windows 10. I remember the frustration caused by not being able to pin folders, which has been fixed. Right-clicking brings a proper menu next to the cursor now, and you can drag icon-tiles if you use the non-fullscreen start menu. It still did suck that those features were gone in Windows 8 in the first place, so I guess that's why it got such bad press.

The layout of applications, folders, and open documents on my screen is more than just an interface, it is a digital representation of how and where my attention is divided. I have skype and netflix running on a second monitor off to the side because I'm keeping an eye on an offline contact and half ignoring some crime drama story while my main monitor is editing 6 different documents in visual studio and moving some files between some folders. Going to anything full screen is like walking into a different room, or flipping my desk over. Suddenly my brain does a mental context switch and I no longer have any idea what I'm working on, just like when you walk into a room and you can't remember why.

Also, a full screen start menu with big colorful moving animated boxes to touch makes my computer feel like a toy, perfect in the form of a tablet with some casual bullshit on it that I'll half pay attention to while doing something else. Except that's how I use my cellphone, not my windows desktop computer.

I have almost never used the start menu in any version of windows (I prefer navigating via windows explorer or short cuts), so the new one greatly increases the time wasted when I accidentally click on the start button instead of the quick icon or bump the windows key on a keyboard.
